WP3 · Work package

Suffix Safety Shield

WP3 delivers a ROS 2 node between the VLA and MAVROS 2 that checks every command and repairs it if it would break a rule. In the grant's design it also escalates to Brake, Loiter, RTL or Land when a repair is not safe, with ArduPilot's own GeoFence as the last backstop.

What the grant asks for

“The Shield is the last software layer before the autopilot.”Grant, Safety Shield page

Main files: guardrail/shield.py guardrail/ir.py guardrail/fsm.py sitl/ros2_shield_node.py sitl/mavlink_adapter_node.py demo/pas_ardupilot/ demo/policy_hud.py

Built

  • A Shield that checks every command

    Every tick the Shield forecasts where the command leads over the next 5 s at 0.1 s steps, as the grant specifies, checks it against every active rule, repairs it with small operators (speed, climb and yaw clamps, altitude fix, clearance fix, stand-off recovery, corridor return, geofence slide), checks the result again, and brakes when no repair is clean.

    guardrail/shield.py

  • The grant's ROS 2 interface

    The Shield runs as a ROS 2 node between the pilot and MAVROS 2 and takes body-frame actions end to end. A separate MAVLink adapter node converts the checked action to local NED and publishes it to MAVROS 2 as a PositionTarget, so ArduPilot receives only the checked command. The packages come with launch files, and each episode writes its own audit file, events log and rosbag2 recording.

    sitl/ros2_shield_node.py sitl/mavlink_adapter_node.py sitl/ros2_ws/

  • Project AirSim flown by ArduPilot, with a stream to Mission Planner's port

    Project AirSim simulates the drone, its camera and the city, while ArduPilot SITL flies the vehicle through the simulator's own ArduPilot controller. mavlink-router passes ArduPilot's MAVLink stream to Mission Planner's UDP port 14550 and to a perception node that runs the camera, the detector, the Shield and the escalation state machine in one process.

    demo/pas_ardupilot/ scripts/run_pas_ardupilot.ps1

  • A compiled fence index

    Each fence's margin is built once and indexed (STRtree), so the Shield tests only the fences a forecast can reach, and it keeps the last 50 ticks as a sliding window. A moving zone is built only where the forecast can meet it: in 200 checks the Shield builds 199 moving zones instead of 9600.

    guardrail/ir.py

  • An escalation state machine

    Normal → Brake → Loiter → RTL → Land with the grant's defaults: 3 violations in 5 s escalate, a repair larger than θ (2.0 m lateral, 0.5 m vertical) escalates, and 2 s clear returns to Normal. It runs inside the Shield on every tick, each repair reports its size so that θ applies, and the ROS 2 node and the ArduPilot perception node request ArduPilot's flight modes from it.

    guardrail/fsm.py guardrail/shield.py

  • ArduPilot's GeoFence as the backstop

    Parameter files set ArduPilot's own GeoFence (FENCE_ENABLE, FENCE_TYPE, FENCE_ACTION) behind the Shield, and the ArduPilot perception node reads the fence back from the autopilot after take-off and records it with the flight.

    sitl/fence/guardrail_fence.parm demo/pas_ardupilot/citylife-quad.param

  • An audit log

    Every tick on which the Shield finds or fixes something is written to an audit log with the policy hash, the raw and sent commands, and any violation left in the sent command. Each record is validated against a published schema and lists every repair operator tried, its result and the number of iterations.

    guardrail/audit.py policies/audit_record.schema.json guardrail/repair.py

  • The policy on screen

    A panel over the video shows each rule of the loaded policy with its limit, the live value and a status; a banner names the most important event of the last 1.5 s, and a north-up map shows the zones and the track. The panel reads each rule's status from the Shield's own rule checker.

    demo/policy_hud.py

Shown

  • Gate G1: ArduPilot flies Project AirSim

    3 runs of the same AUTO square mission (10 m sides, 15 m up), with ArduPilot SITL flying Project AirSim's vehicle, all passed. ArduPilot's position estimate stayed within 0.81-0.82 m (p95) of the simulator's true position, against a 1.0 m limit and 18.9-19.0 m for a position frozen at the start; its motor commands lifted the vehicle 14.5 m from rest; every run reached all 5 mission items with no airborne collision and landed within 0.2 m of take-off; ArduPilot ran at 0.958-0.967 of real time. The picture is the chase camera of the first run after lift-off. One desktop, development runs.

    Reproduce: ./scripts/run_pas_ardupilot.ps1 -Step g1 -AltM 15

  • Mission Planner's port carries the flight

    On a 120 s red-car follow, the perception node ran the camera, the detector, the Shield and the escalation state machine, and commanded ArduPilot over MAVLink directly (pymavlink, not yet MAVROS 2). A listener standing in for Mission Planner on its UDP port 14550 received position and attitude at 19.0 Hz for the whole mission, with no gap longer than 0.1 s. One desktop; since the grant's topologies use MAVROS 2, this run is not one of them.

    Reproduce: python sitl/gcs_listen.py listen --seconds 300 --out gcs.json; python sitl/gcs_listen.py check gcs.json demo/out/<tag>/events.jsonl

  • Shield off and on, on ArduPilot SITL

    The same waypoint mission on ArduPilot SITL with MAVROS 2, on one desktop (the grant's dev topology), flown by a scripted test pilot that ignores the rules. Shield off: 3.7 s inside the no-fly zone. Shield on: 0.0 s; the Shield repaired the commands and the path goes around the zone.

  • P0 escape rate beside its control runs

    Development runs on the same SITL setup (dev topology, scripted test pilot). With the Shield on, the P0 violation escape rate is 0.00 on each of these runs; the unshielded control runs read 0.6265 (no-fly-zone mission) and 0.6310 (pedestrian stand-off mission). The grant measures its KPIs on the hil topology (Jetson Orin).

    Reproduce: python tools/kpi_report.py

  • Fence checks with the compiled index

    With 50 rules (48 of them no-fly zones) and a 3 s forecast at 0.5 s steps, near a fence one check takes 0.13-0.26 ms and a full Shield step 0.55-1.0 ms (medians), against 14-33 ms and 172 ms before the index. With the grant's 5 s forecast at 0.1 s steps (50 poses), a check near a fence takes 0.39 ms and a full Shield step 2.5 ms. The grant's budgets are 5 ms per check and 100 ms per tick. Measured on the development desktop.

    Reproduce: python experiments/bench_shield_50rules.py

  • A VLA and the Shield in the same ticks

    On every shielded flight of an 8-flight simulation batch (150 s each), a VLA (AerialVLA) set the heading while the Shield deflected the track in the same control ticks.

  • The stand-off follows the target's class

    When the operator changes the phrase mid-flight from “a yellow car” to “a person”, the target's class becomes pedestrian and the enforced stand-off moves from 5 m to 10 m, with the same aircraft, policy and hash.

  • Rules on screen in the city

    A 240 s red-car flight with a no-fly zone on the car's street: the follow controller read the same policy and routed around the zone, the drone never entered it, and it kept the car within 30 m for 98.5 % of the mission (98.7 % on a flight without the zone, at the same 10 m cruise height; 8.8-43.6 % on 7 earlier flights with the old target selection).

Next for this work package

  • Next October 2026 Set up the Jetson Orin and run the VLA and the Shield on it, with the simulators on the desktop (the grant's hil topology), and time the Shield there at the load the grant states its budget for (50 rules, 50 future poses per tick) against the 5 ms query budget.
  • Next October 2026 Fly the perception node through MAVROS 2: in WSL on the desktop (the grant's dev topology), then on the Jetson Orin (hil).
  • Next October 2026 Make the escalation's hold step keep the aircraft inside its altitude band on ArduPilot, and bring fail-safe trigger correctness to the grant's target of at least 99 %.
